title: ByteSize validation: huge numeric strings must raise ValidationError, not OverflowError
answers: ByteSize crashes with OverflowError on a very long number
cannot convert float infinity to integer in ByteSize validation
why does a huge byte size string not produce a ValidationError
how should custom type validators handle numeric overflow
body:
Symptom: validating a `ByteSize` field with an absurdly long number (e.g. '1'*310 + 'KB') raised a raw `OverflowError` instead of a normal ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/types.py:ByteSize._validate does `int(float(scalar) * unit_mult)`. `float()` of a 310-digit string becomes `inf`, and `int(inf)` raises OverflowError. Only ValueError/AssertionError/PydanticCustomError get turned into validation errors, so the OverflowError escaped.
Fix pattern: wrap the conversion in `try/except OverflowError` and re-raise `PydanticCustomError('byte_size', 'could not parse value and unit from byte string')`. This reuses the error type and message already used for unparseable byte strings.
Constraints: this applies to any validator in pydantic/types.py that converts user input through float→int (or other arithmetic that can overflow). It must raise PydanticCustomError with an existing error type, not a new type. `byte_sizes` is now annotated `dict[str, float]`. Tests live in tests/test_types.py:test_bytesize_raises and match on the message ('parse value').
applies: pydantic/types.py ByteSize and similar custom-type validators that do numeric conversion on user input
